family and I have been coming to this practice for over 35 years and have always had an excellent service.  I used to brag to all of my friends about how good it was and the receptionists were always so helpful.  Unfortunately this is not the case any more.  All of the familiar friendly faces have left and the new ones are not at all helpful.
The doctors and nurses are excellent but getting an appointment is a nightmare.
Our recent experience is with my husband who had been awake in the night with a badly swollen face and lips.  He called first thing this morning to get an appointment and was told he would be triaged with a nurse.  He did not receive a call only a text to refer him to the pharmacy.  This wasn't until past 1pm.  He did what was advised but the pharmacist said he did know why he was sent to him.  He told him to go to A & E.
We try to do the right thing for the hospital by not wasting their time unnecessarily but it seems pointless having a GP if you can't see them.
Such a shame that this has happened after all of these years!

As is usual now with most practices, we operate a triage system to enable the right person to deal with the issue. It does not have to be the GP anymore, there are a variety of different skilled health professionals to treat patients nowadays. Pharmacies have been funded to provide extended services to reduce the pressure on GP practices and can treat and prescribe for some conditions so if we triage to a pharmacy, the decision was based on the information provided. It would be very helpful to know the pharmacy involved so I can follow up this feedback. I will look at the decision making to see if there was anything that could have been done differently. Unfortunately demand is so much higher these days and outstrips capacity. We do our utmost to ensure everyone is dealt with appropriately although not everyone may agree with the decision. We used to only give on the day appointments but more people expected same day than we could accommodate. It doesn't mean we are a bad practice, but we do have to allocate our time according to need.  Regarding your comments on our staff at reception, yes some are new and learning every day. It takes time to be accustomed to so many different ailments. Some staff retired but new staff are just as lovely and I am more than satisfied with their progress into GP practice life which is hugely demanding. As with most surgeries we don't always get it right for many reasons but we acknowledge where we may have gone wrong and do what we can to rectify it. Primary Care is overwhelmed and has seen a significant increase in demand with little government funding to match pace. We strive to give a good service in the face of many challenges. Triage process helps manage some of those demands but always with patient safety when making clinical decisions. We absolutely understand why you have given this feedback and we will review our actions. If you want to email the practice to follow up this review, that would be great. Please contact us if the pharmacy were not able to help today. Thank you, Philip Practice Manager. 

Addendum 14/1/26 from what I can see the pharmacist carried out a full consult, and treatment provided with follow up advice to seek NHS111 or 999 as red flag safety netting advice after the consultation. The pharmacy did not record that this was inappropriate for them to deal with nor that they told you to go to A&E. I do believe this was appropriate and supportive. As with a lot of processes nowadays, a text was sent to go to pharmacy with a confirmation that we had pre-booked to the pharmacy so they knew about the case.  This was a same day response and appropriate for the condition.  The pharmacy were advised by yourselves that the condition had been ongoing for three weeks.  I do not believe that we acted inappropriately or with any undue delay.  I am sorry you had cause to feedback as you have but this really was a quick response. Although you were asked on the 5/9 to make a routine appointment, I can't see that one has actually been booked yet.  We strive to ensure routine appointments are offered within two to three weeks however demand has risen and this is currently at four weeks waiting time for the appointment but we hope to bring that down in the near future.  The demand on general practice is increasing and with limited resources GP Practices are under a huge strain.  We are experiencing a significant increase in demand for appointments, queries and prescriptions. We apologise as this can lead to a delay in answering the telephone or being able to offer appointments and advice in a timely manner.

We are trying to improve access to the surgery for you with new ways of delivering services. Whilst trying to deal with each telephone request appropriately we are limited by the lack of government investment into general practice to meet some of the time demands.

Problems faced by all practices across England:

1.	The NHS budget for 2024/25 will grow by 0.2%, well below inflation.
2.	Government investment in primary care has fallen from 8.9% (2015/16) to less than 7% (2024/25). This is equivalent to a 7% cut in funding.
3.	Your practice receives just £107.57 per year for each patient, or 30 pence per day - less than the cost of an apple.
4.	The Government and Integrated Care Boards are increasing the demand on general practice by moving more work from secondary care into the community.
5.	The overall population in England is increasing - 53.5 million in 2012 to 57.1 million in 2022.
6.	There are fewer GPs due to funding limits. There are 1759 fewer fully qualified full-time GPs compared to 2015. As a result, each full-time GP is responsible for 356 more patients than in 2015.
7.	GPs need to supervise other clinical staff, which can reduce appointment availability.
8.	People are living longer with more complex health and social care needs.
9.	Some GP surgeries are having to close or merge to maintain services to patients.

We are aware that patient satisfaction with the NHS is falling, with difficulty calling GP surgeries a particular problem.

We are trying our best to provide the service our patients need, but the current staffing and funding crisis felt across general practice in England is severely restricting what we can offer in the timescales NHS England suggests.

Thank you for your understanding.
